name: Pembrolizumab plus Platinum and Infusional Fluorouracil (KEYNOTE-048), First-Line Recurrent or Metastatic Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma, then Pembrolizumab Maintenance
disease: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (non-nasopharyngeal)

biomarkers.PD_L1: PD-L1 selection not required for the pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy combination (used across CPS strata, including PD-L1 negative disease)
biomarkers.note: Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers v2.2026, SYST-A 4 of 7, pembrolizumab plus platinum plus infusional fluorouracil is a first-line Preferred option (category 1) with no PD-L1 threshold; the Discussion (MS-56) states there is no PD-L1-based selection for the combination of chemotherapy and pembrolizumab, and the combination may be particularly suitable for patients with a large disease burden or nearing a clinical crisis. Contrast with pembrolizumab monotherapy, which requires CPS at least 1 (see hn-pembro-mono).

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: recurrent, unresectable, or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma with no surgical or radiotherapy option
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: pembrolizumab plus cisplatin or carboplatin plus infusional fluorouracil
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, SYST-A 4 of 7 (First-Line Preferred: Carboplatin/Infusional Fluorouracil + Pembrolizumab and Cisplatin/Infusional Fluorouracil + Pembrolizumab, category 1)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: non-nasopharyngeal primary; nasopharynx follows a separate systemic-therapy pathway (NASO-B)
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, SYST-A 1 of 7 (Principles of Systemic Therapy for Non-Nasopharyngeal Cancers header)

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
provenance.locator: Discussion MS-59 (pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks; alternate 400 mg every 6 weeks); indication SYST-A 4 of 7 (first-line Preferred, category 1)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, Discussion MS-59. Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV flat dose on day 1 every 21 days. Source-stated alternate schedule: 400 mg IV every 42 days. Flat milligram dosing (basis flat), not mg/kg. Given with platinum/fluorouracil during the chemotherapy phase, then continued as maintenance monotherapy until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: line 58325 (recurrent or metastatic Wayne State regimen: cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV recycled every 3 weeks)

drugs.notes: CISplatin 100 mg/m2 IV on day 1 every 21 days. The 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks value is sourced to DeVita 12th ed. (line 58325), the recurrent or metastatic Wayne State cisplatin plus 5-fluorouracil regimen, matching the platinum dose used in the recurrent/metastatic KEYNOTE-048 combination. Source-stated platinum alternative: CARBOplatin dosed by target AUC (AUC value not established in the cited sources; requires verification). ISMP tall-man applied.

drugs.name: Fluorouracil (infusional)

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

drugs.notes: Infusional fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m2 per day by continuous IV infusion over 96 hours (days 1 to 4), recycled every 3 weeks, is grounded to DeVita 12th ed. line 58326 to 58327 (the recurrent or metastatic Wayne State cisplatin plus 5-fluorouracil regimen), which is the platinum/fluorouracil backbone used with pembrolizumab in KEYNOTE-048. DPYD deficiency substantially increases fluoropyrimidine toxicity; consider DPYD testing before treatment.

supportiveCare: Antiemetic prophylaxis for the cisplatin-containing cycles: high emetic risk (cisplatin); prophylaxis per emetogenicity tier.
Immune-related adverse event surveillance for pembrolizumab (thyroid, hepatic, pulmonary, colitis, dermatologic, endocrine).
Fluoropyrimidine safety: consider DPYD genotyping before fluorouracil; reduce or avoid in DPYD deficiency.
G-CSF / febrile-neutropenia risk assessment per institutional practice (VERIFY: not established in the cited sources for this regimen).

monitoring: renal function (creatinine/GFR) before each cisplatin dose
immune-related toxicity screen (TSH/free T4, LFTs, glucose, cortisol as indicated) during pembrolizumab
Mucositis and diarrhea assessment - infusional fluorouracil
imaging every 2 to 3 cycles in the recurrent/metastatic setting (Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, SYST-A 1 of 7 general principles)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold pembrolizumab and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; obtain clinical review before rechallenge.

doseModificationRules.condition: renal impairment or cytopenia on day 1
doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Protocol-specific delay/reduce criteria may apply; physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: recurrent or metastatic cisplatin 100 mg/m2 and 5-fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m2 per day over 96 hours recycled every 3 weeks (Wayne State regimen, lines 58325 to 58327)

core.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22nd ed.
core.locator: Head and Neck Cancer chapter (lines 88286 to 88299): pembrolizumab compared as single agent and in combination with cisplatin and 5-FU versus prior standard chemotherapy; combination pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy favored for lower PD-L1 expression

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
guideline.locator: SYST-A 4 of 7 (Recurrent, Unresectable, or Metastatic Disease, First-Line Preferred: Carboplatin or Cisplatin/Infusional Fluorouracil + Pembrolizumab, category 1); dosing Discussion MS-59; KEYNOTE-048 Discussion MS-55 to MS-56 (no PD-L1-based selection for the combination)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for the KEYNOTE-048 chemoimmunotherapy regimen (pembrolizumab plus cisplatin or carboplatin plus infusional fluorouracil, then pembrolizumab maintenance) in first-line recurrent or metastatic non-nasopharyngeal head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Serves the squamous-cell head and neck sites (reference sites #32 to 39 and #41), not nasopharynx (separate NASO-B pathway) and not salivary gland (#40, separate protocol). The regimen identity and category 1 first-line Preferred status, and the absence of a PD-L1 selection requirement for the combination, are from Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026 SYST-A 4 of 7 and Discussion MS-56. Pembrolizumab flat 200 mg IV every 21 days (alternate 400 mg every 42 days) is sourced to Discussion MS-59. CISplatin 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks is sourced to DeVita 12th ed. line 58325 (the recurrent or metastatic Wayne State cisplatin plus 5-fluorouracil regimen). Infusional Fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m2 per day by continuous infusion over 96 hours (days 1 to 4), recycled every 3 weeks, is grounded to DeVita 12th ed. lines 58326 to 58327 (the same Wayne State recurrent or metastatic regimen). The NCCN SYST-A pages do not print per-drug mg/m2 doses, and the cited sources do not state a KEYNOTE-048-specific number of platinum/fluorouracil chemotherapy cycles or the carboplatin target AUC for the cisplatin-ineligible alternative, so regimen.cycles and the carboplatin AUC alternative remain VERIFY (the AUC is noted on the cisplatin entry). ISMP tall-man applied (CISplatin, CARBOplatin). Setting recurrent/metastatic, palliative intent, first-line. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
